title: Version-pin circuit design notes
content:
Purpose
---
Notes and working design for treating model-version pinning as a set of "circuits" in the control plane that can be enabled/disabled, probed, and tripped by runtime routing. Goal: make pinning semantics explicit, robust in multi-region topologies, and observable so applications can reason about degradation and fallback behavior.

High-level idea (metaphor)
---
Treat each (client, model-family, version) pin as a logical circuit with three axes: affinity, compatibility, and health. Circuits can be: CLOSED (route counts honored), OPEN (no routing to pinned version; fallback paths used), or HALF-OPEN (probing, canary traffic allowed). Control plane manages circuit state and publishes to routers. Routers enforce routing rules with TTLs and local caches.

Why this helps
---
- Makes failure modes explicit (e.g., pinned version unhealthy vs. incompatible).
- Allows automated safe fallback when a pinned version can’t serve (graceful fallbacks instead of 500s).
- Enables canary-style rollouts of revisions while preserving pin guarantees for critical customers.

Key components
---
1) Pin registry: authoritative mapping (customer:pin)-> {version, created_at, owner, policy}. Lightweight, control-plane-only.
2) Circuit controller: derives circuit state from health checks, compatibility signals, and staleness windows. Publishes deltas.
3) Router policy engine: consumes circuit state and routing hints to make per-request decisions. Local caches with TTL and changefeed subscription.
4) Compatibility evaluator: scores runtime compatibility between a pinned model version and available variants (quantized / fp16 / cpu-sim). Produces numerical score + reason codes.
5) Observability surface: per-pin timeline, last-success, failure counts, fallback actions, and incident flags.

State machine (sketch)
---
- CLOSED: default when pin is active and compatibility >= threshold and recent successes > X. Route precedence to pinned version.
- HALF-OPEN: enter when we detect a transient issue (rate of errors spikes) OR during controlled rollout. Allow a fixed probe rate (e.g., 1%) to pinned version while routing remainder to fallback.
- OPEN: enter when pinned version fails compatibility checks or sustained health fails beyond drift window. Fallback routing used for all traffic. Set automation to attempt recovery.

Compatibility scoring (proposal)
---
We want a compact 0..100 score. Inputs: model-arch match, tokenizer/version, quantization mode, KV cache layout, kernel availability on target hardware, max-context support, serialization format, breaking-config flags.
Score components (weights, example):
- Arch match (40)
- Tokenizer/IO match (20)
- Runtime kernel availability (15)
- KV/cache layout (10)
- Quantization compatibility (10)
- Misc flags (5)

Interpretation: >=80 = compatible; 50-79 = degraded compatibility (allow HALF-OPEN/probe with warnings); <50 = incompatible (OPEN). We store a short reason code list for the top 3 mismatches to populate UI and operator alerts.

Multi-region considerations
---
- Circuit state is global but routers maintain region-local caches. Control plane publishes region-scoped deltas when there are region-only impacts (e.g., specific GPU pool offline).
- Pins should support per-region overrides. Default is global pin, but ops/sales can set region pin exemptions (e.g., EU pinned to v1.2, US fallback to compatible v1.1) — these are separate circuits.
- Sync window: allow router caches TTL of 10s for fast failover, but publish sticky notification channels for critical pins. In contexts where strict locality is required, TTL can be tuned down to 1s at the cost of increased control-plane load.

Failure modes and mitigations
---
1) Control-plane partition: routers keep prior state and enter stale-protect mode (continue honoring last-known CLOSED pins for a short grace window). After grace window, if circuit state not refreshed, transition to HALF-OPEN with aggressive probing disabled.
2) Rapid incompatible rollout: compatibility evaluator marks many pins incompatible at once (e.g., new kernel rollout). Use staggered re-eval and rate-limited notification to avoid thrashing; expose batch-change preview to product owners.
3) Region outage: for pins with strict region-local data residency, OPEN may be the correct behavior. We must ensure SLA docs reflect this tradeoff.

Routing precedence rules (simple algorithm)
---
Given request R with key K (customer, model-family):
1) Check region-scoped pin circuits for (K, region). If CLOSED -> route to pinned variant.
2) Else check global pin circuits for (K). If CLOSED -> route to pinned variant.
3) If circuit is HALF-OPEN -> route small N% to pinned variant, rest to fallback. Adjust sampling by customer tier.
4) If OPEN or incompatible -> route to best compatible variant per compatibility score and policy (cost vs latency).
5) If no compatible variant -> failover to degrade-mode (short response with error code + fallback suggestion).

Operational signals and dashboards
---
- Per-pin SLOs: last N calls' success rate, p95 latency delta vs. baseline, fallback ratio.
- Health timeline: chart of CLOSED/HALF-OPEN/OPEN over time with event annotations.
- Compatibility histogram: distribution of top reason codes across all pins (e.g., tokenizers mismatches are 40%).
- Alert rules: when pinned failure rate > 2% for 5m -> Pager for oncall; when >10% 15m -> Incident.

Rollout playbook (operators)
---
- Intentional upgrade: create new pin for canary group -> set pin circuit to HALF-OPEN with probe=5% -> monitor SLOs 1h -> escalate to CLOSED if stable.
- Emergency rollback: set pin circuit to OPEN for affected customers -> schedule recovery window and root-cause analysis.
- Bulk migration: use staggered region waves, publish predicted compatibility scores and auto-fallback mapping to owners before enactment.

Open questions / TODOs
---
- TTL vs control-plane QPS tradeoffs: quantify the cost of 1s vs 10s router TTL at scale (cost model + load tests).
- Backward-compatibility tests: what unit/integration tests should run pre-pinning to ensure score alignment? (linked: github:infra/tests#78)
- How do we represent partial compatibility (e.g., supports inference but not streaming) in score and routing decision?
- UX: surface reason codes concisely to customers without leaking infra details.

Appendix: quick compatibility sample table (human readable)
---
Columns: pinned_version | candidate_variant | arch-match | kernels | tokenizer | quant-match | score | recommended-action
Rows (examples):
v1.2.0 | v1.2.0-fp16 | yes | yes | yes | partial | 93 | route
v1.2.0 | v1.1.9-quant | yes | partial | yes | yes | 72 | half-open/probe
v1.2.0 | v2.0.0 | no | no | no | no | 18 | incompatible/open

Closing notes
---
This doc is intentionally lightweight — the next step is a small prototype: control-plane simulation that can ingest a set of pins, candidate variants (with synthetic compatibility vectors), and replay region outages to validate state transitions and router cache behavior. I propose a 2‑week spike owned by platform-engineering to produce the prototype and a follow-up doc with concrete API payloads and event schemas.
